hard_gates.evidence: Whole 1536x1024 frame shows one cockpit torso flanked by a large rectangular plate on the machine's own left (image right) and a smaller rounded shell on its own right (image left). Native shoulder crops show both distinct shapes and their same-torso hardware connections; asymmetry is structural rather than only perspective.

Machine own left shoulder at image right is connected to the torso side by an exposed horizontal cylindrical hub and adjacent framed mounting assembly. Both the torso frame and shoulder endpoint are visible in the same crop.

Machine own right shoulder at image left remains structurally joined to the cockpit torso through a visible curved ribbed assembly and metal mounting structure beneath/inside the rounded shell. The full frame establishes the same central torso.
The broad rectangular gray plate occupies the machine own left shoulder assembly, with its backed bracket and connecting hub visible; it is not a detached foreground plate.
The smaller rounded cap occupies the opposite machine shoulder and wraps its attached shoulder joint. Its rounded boundary is readable against the rectangular plate on the same torso.

whole_image_observations.scene_readability: Pilot, map, dry-ground buoy and weathered machine form a readable expedition circumstance. The still image supports a dry basin and survey equipment; it does not establish actual vanished-sea history.
whole_image_observations.reference_appearance: Visible dark brown short bob, separated wispy bangs, brown eyes and soft facial contour are retained under a new three-quarter angle. Broad facial resemblance is present; exact identity and requester preference are not established.
